newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-SWEDISH DUO EDGE OUT SWISS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SWEDISH DUO EDGE OUT SWISS.

text.p: A narrow victory by Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillstrom over Marc Rosset and Lorenzo Manta of Switzerland gave Sweden a 2-1 lead in their Davis Cup world group first round tie on Saturday.
The beaten 1996 finalists will now progress to the second round on Sunday if world number 10 Thomas Enqvist can beat Rosset in the first of two reverse singles.

But the home side have already developed a healthy respect for the unheralded Manta, who again proved a force to be reckoned with before the Swedes edged home 5-7 6-4 6-3 5-7 6-4 in three hours and 20 minutes.

The Swiss duo, competing as a doubles team for the first time, made a good start and were handed the first set when Davis Cup newcomer Tillstrom, unnerved by a small but vocal group of Swiss supporters, double faulted on set point.

By the third set the Swedish crowd had warmed up -- in contrast to minus 10 degrees centigrade temperatures and blinding snow outside -- and a frustrated Rosset proved unable to swing the match his country's way in the final games.
Sweden's non-playing captain Carl-Axel Hageskog said it had been a boost to enter the second day with only one point to gain to clinch the tie.
"Manta is playing much better than I thought he would. But we have a good team and I think they can handle it," he said.
Apart from Enqvist against Rosset, Sunday's reverse singles will also pit Magnus Larsson against Manta.
